A lot of the time it was a real struggle to keep it coherent,
it was a struggle to be coherent.
The problem was that I could no longer distinguish
between my life and the stuff I was writing.
Everything got blurred.
You could only tell one from the other when I was actually doing one or the other,
but then it was too late.
I would wake up at night in a cold sweat,
my throat suddenly dry, my body tense.
This was the time when I felt most alive,
and I would start to write in my journal.

Every day, I would wake up and wonder:
What would I write about today?
This is how life got to be like a novel.
It wasn't something I was doing to a real thing,
it was just what life felt like.
I couldn't separate it from the writing,
or from the things I said.
I would be going along fine,
and someone would ask me if I was all right,
and I would reply with a line from the book,
and I would know they would have to wait while I wrote it down,
and it would be a while before I could continue the conversation.
I was writing the book.

The problem was, I knew it wasn't any good.
It was just all over the place.
I had trouble getting it into the right shape,
I just didn't know where I was going.
I knew that it was like having an incomplete file
to work on, but I didn't have a sense of where the missing bits were.
It wasn't like a missing section of a book,
it was more like a missing part of my head,
where the plot was hidden.
I started to read other books,
because I thought they might give me some ideas about what to do next,
and eventually I got the sense that everyone else's books were just as incomplete as mine.

Some of the things I wrote were actually about life,
and they did have a shape.
I found that I could take a line of mine and it would go right back to the place where it started.
It was all one story, and everything fit together.
I didn't know how I could tell what was true and what wasn't.
I just couldn't tell the difference, it was all true,
all of it.
I wanted to tell the truth, I wanted to be true to myself,
and I would write something down, but it would feel so true that it was like being naked in front of everybody,
and I didn't know how I could ever take it back.
I would get to the point where I couldn't see straight,
I would feel like a complete moron.
I was terrified, I was scared.
I couldn't do it any more, I couldn't take the pressure.
I would just delete my journal entries,
and pretend I was never going to write another word.
I would close my laptop and get the hell away from the keyboard.
I would go for a walk, or go to bed early,
and try to forget the whole thing.

I didn't know what to do,
I didn't know how to write,
I didn't know how to be alive.
